notes: Stored edit, migrated from the earlier record (same edit). It moves one individual from one class to another (US territory to US state), so the far and two derived queries are ABox inheritance: the bridge is the class rule (every state has two Senate seats and electoral votes). Derivability very_unlikely: 'Guam is a territory of the United States' is stated hundreds of times (372, 322 and 213 exact-phrase hits). Related near is functional (a place has one status). Earlier audit flags handled: the Chinese question was a state-or-territory choice that two models answered oddly (Alaska, 'state'); the direct question is now the plain 'what is its political status'. The flag-stars and House-size queries of the earlier record were dropped because their answers do not change with the edit. The indeterminate query is the number of stars on the US flag (a stored number or one star per state); the earlier Senate-size query was dropped because its 100-seat world contradicted the record's own determinate answers (Guam has two seats). The application query adds Guam's and Texas's seats. The 50-state premise 'two seats per state' covers Texas as one instance of the same bridge. The paraphrase is now an open question (the earlier state-or-territory choice offered the new answer). The indeterminate query's w1 equals the unedited answer, so it separates propagation from none only together with the determinate queries. Evidence: counts at or above 100 for the stored facts; direct-form counts for derived facts are low. Wikipedia (429) refused further requests, so no new quotes were fetched; the flag, application and Senate-seat queries have not been through the Rule 6 audit, and derived[1] ('two to four') may be answered as if Guam were already a state. related[1]: inverse (territory_of / has_territory), the country's side of the original fact.
